prerequisites: Controlled Windows10 machine; preserve existing settings and registration; ordinary local file selection.
reproduce.title: Compare registration and Explorer activation for both classic handlers
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys0.103.3012 as reported versus current stable on Windows10
reproduce.expected_result: Both enabled classic menu entries appear and launch for the same Explorer user; otherwise the first failed registration/load boundary is identified.
steps: 1. Confirm both modules enabled; restart PowerToys and record registration outcomes.
2. Right-click a newly created local text file, not an empty folder background, and record whether each menu entry appears.
3. Compare same-user standard/elevated runs and a normal Explorer restart; capture read-only classic-handler registration and load results.
4. Add the sanitized failing boundary and newer-release result to48951, keeping the Windows11/ARM64 symptom separate.
setup: Use the reported per-user install; compare PowerToys running standard versus elevated under the same signed-in Explorer user. Do not mix release DLLs or apply speculative registry repairs.

evidence: The reporter says both File Locksmith and PowerRename are absent from Windows 10 File Explorer context menus on PowerToys0.103.3012, GitHub per-user installation, running elevated.

The supplied diagnostic archive was inspected: both modules are enabled in settings, PowerRename repeatedly logs enabled and context-menu registered, and the installer reports successful completion with no Return value3.
A registration-success log does not prove Explorer loaded the handler. No shell activation trace or same-user registration snapshot establishes the failed boundary.
Open issue48951 already covers both missing entries on Windows10 after the runtime-registration transition; its separate Windows11/ARM64 discussion must not be treated as this report root cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate with48951 and reproduce the Windows10 classic-shell registration/loading boundary.
judgment.rationale: Consolidate this newer release and supplied diagnostic evidence with the existing Windows10 shell-registration investigation. The evidence rules out simply assuming the modules are disabled or that installation failed, but does not prove a specific registry repair.
